title: From Rome: Half-Day Frascati Wine Tour with Farmhouse Lunch

galleryImages.alt: Wine bottles and tasting glasses on a table beside the farmhouse vines
A glass of white wine during an outdoor farmhouse tasting
A plated farmhouse lunch served beside a glass of wine
Wine bottles displayed in the historic farmhouse cellar

abstract: Walk through Frascati, taste three wines at a family farmhouse, and settle in for a chef-prepared lunch. Meet in Frascati; local winery transfers are included.
highlights: A town walk before the vines — discover Frascati with an English-speaking guide and a local tasting stop.
A family farmhouse in the countryside — follow the wine story from vineyard rows to the old cellar.
Three wines to compare — a guided farmhouse tasting puts different local styles side by side.
A proper pause for lunch — sit down to the chef’s meal at the farmhouse after your tasting.
Local journeys taken care of — travel between Frascati and the farmhouse with the operator.
A sociable half-day — combine time outdoors, wine conversation and a shared meal in one reservation.
includes: Guided town visit — an English-speaking guide introduces the historic centre before the farmhouse visit.
Town tasting — local wine and a traditional snack are included on the Frascati walking portion.
Local transfers — the operator takes you from Frascati to the farmhouse and back to the station.
Vineyard and cellar visit — see the farmhouse’s wine setting with a guided introduction on site.
Three-wine tasting — the farmhouse visit includes a guided tasting of three boutique wines.
Farmhouse lunch — a chef-prepared meal is served at the farmhouse as part of your booking.
excludes: Train tickets between Rome and Frascati.
meetingPoint: Outside Frascati railway station, behind the yellow taxi stand, Piazzale Sandro Pertini. Follow the time and meeting instructions on your booking confirmation.
notSuitableFor: Wheelchair users, according to the activity listing.
goodToKnow: The experience starts in Frascati, despite “From Rome” in its title.
Book rail travel separately and check the current timetable; suggested trains differ by day.
Ask the operator about dietary needs before booking; do not assume that every menu can be adapted.
fullDescription: This is a town-and-country wine outing for visitors who want more than a tasting counter. The opening walk introduces Frascati before the group leaves town for a family farmhouse. A wine-and-snack stop gives the first part of the day its own food focus, so the experience does not depend entirely on the later winery visit.

At the farmhouse, the vineyard and old cellar provide the setting for a guided comparison of three wines. The experience finishes around the table with the chef’s lunch. Choose this format if conversation, a local meal and a sense of place matter as much as tasting notes. It is a shared experience rather than an exclusive winery appointment.

Plan the journey from Rome as a separate part of your day. The operator’s transfers run between Frascati and the farmhouse; the advertised four hours are the activity duration, not a promise about the complete journey from your accommodation. Keep your afternoon flexible enough for the train back.

faq.q: Does this tour pick me up in Rome?
faq.a: No. Meet outside Frascati station. Transfers between Frascati and the farmhouse are included; train tickets from Rome are separate.
Yes. The listing includes a chef-prepared farmhouse lunch and a guided three-wine tasting.
The listing states that this activity is not suitable for wheelchair users.

title: From Rome: Pasta Masterclass & Wine Tour in the Vineyard

abstract: Make three traditional pasta shapes with a chef, explore the farmhouse vineyard and cellar, then enjoy wine tasting and lunch. Local station transfers are included; Rome trains are separate.
highlights: Make ravioli, fettuccine and maltagliati with guidance from the farmhouse chef.
Compare local wines and extra-virgin olive oil with an English-speaking wine guide.
Visit the vineyards and old cellar before sitting down to your lunch.
Choose a practical cooking experience rather than a town walking tour.
includes: Pasta class — the chef guides preparation of three local pasta varieties at the farmhouse.
Wine and olive-oil tasting — sample the farmhouse’s wines and extra-virgin olive oil during the visit.
Vineyard and cellar tour — learn about the property alongside an English-speaking licensed wine taster.
Chef lunch — eat the pasta prepared during the class with accompanying food and wine.
Station transfers — car or minivan transport links the station and farmhouse for guests arriving by train.
excludes: Train tickets to and from Rome.
meetingPoint: Normally outside Frascati station. The listing gives different Saturday instructions via Tor Vergata; confirm your exact station with the operator for your date.
goodToKnow: The advertised small group is limited to 15 participants.
The listing offers dietary adaptations on request; tell the operator when booking.
Saturday arrival instructions differ from other days. Check your confirmation before buying train tickets.
fullDescription: The cooking class gives your half-day a hands-on centre. Instead of spending the opening portion walking around Frascati, you travel to the farmhouse and work with its chef. Ravioli, fettuccine and maltagliati are the three pasta varieties described by the operator, making the class useful for visitors who want to practise more than one shape.

Wine remains part of the experience, with a tasting, olive oil, and a visit to the old cellar and vineyard. Lunch then brings the cooking and tasting elements together. This is one combined product: you do not need to buy a separate winery reservation to receive the experiences listed here.

The activity is listed as four hours with a maximum of 15 participants. Travel from Rome is your responsibility. The operator supplies the local station-to-farmhouse journeys, but its Saturday instructions name Tor Vergata for arrival. Confirm the meeting station for your date instead of assuming it matches another Frascati tour.

faq.q: Are the cooking class and wine tour booked together?
faq.a: Yes. This listing includes both, plus lunch and local station transfers.
Frascati is the normal meeting station, but the listing gives a different Saturday arrival at Tor Vergata. Confirm the instructions for your booking.
The listing invites requests for vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free adaptations. Get confirmation for your specific needs before booking.

title: Rome Countryside: Wine Tasting Tour with Private Driver

abstract: A countryside vineyard visit with wine-and-food pairings and a private driver from Rome. Pickup and drop-off are included; confirm the collection address for your booking.
highlights: Leave the rail planning to a private driver with pickup and return in Rome.
Visit a countryside vineyard and wine cellar on a guided outing.
Taste wines with local food pairings in a compact three-hour itinerary.
Keep transport private while checking how the winery tasting itself is hosted.
includes: Return transport — pickup, a private driver and drop-off are included in this Rome departure.
Vineyard and cellar visit — the guided experience introduces the wine setting and production story.
Wine tasting — sample a selection of wines with explanations during the visit.
Food pairings — snacks accompany the tasting; the listing does not promise a full lunch.
meetingPoint: Pickup in Rome. Confirm the eligible collection address and time with Rome Grand Tour after choosing your date.
goodToKnow: The listing offers English, Italian and Spanish; check the language available for your selected departure.
Wear comfortable shoes because the visit includes walking.
A private driver does not by itself guarantee exclusive use of the winery or tasting room.
fullDescription: This format suits visitors who would rather begin with collection in Rome than organise a regional train. Rome Grand Tour includes a private driver, pickup and drop-off, together with a vineyard and cellar visit in the countryside. Its advertised itinerary allows roughly three hours for the outing, including the road journeys.

At the winery, wines are served with local food pairings. The reservation includes snacks rather than a promised farmhouse lunch, so decide whether you want a short tasting excursion or a meal-focused day before comparing prices. The guide introduces the wines and the cellar setting; the exact venue and arrangements should be checked with the operator.

The practical advantage is the transport. Provide your accommodation address and confirm collection eligibility, departure time and language before relying on the booking. If exclusive tasting-room access matters for a celebration, request that detail explicitly: private transport and a fully private winery visit are different arrangements.

faq.a: Yes. The listing includes pickup, private-driver transport and drop-off. Confirm your address and time with the operator.
The stated inclusion is snacks paired with wine, not a full lunch.
The listing specifies a private group and driver, but do not infer exclusive use of the winery. Confirm the tasting arrangements with the operator.
